html:
A Buddhist monastery at the foot of Mount Song in Henan, China, founded in 495 under the Northern Wei dynasty for an Indian monk named Batuo.

Legend links it with Bodhidharma, the Indian monk said to have sat facing a cave wall nearby for nine years and to be the founder of Chan (Zen) Buddhism. The story was written down much later, but it made Shaolin a holy place of Chan.

Its fame for fighting is better documented. Monks helped Li Shimin, the future Tang emperor Taizong, in the wars of the 620s and were rewarded with land. By the Ming period Shaolin monks were known for staff fighting and were called up against pirates. Shaolin kung fu grew into a style taught across China.

The temple was burned in 1928 during the warlord years, and many buildings date from after that. Kung fu films from the 1980s brought crowds back, and it is now a large school and tourist site.
sum: A Buddhist monastery at the foot of Mount Song in Henan, China, founded in 495 under the Northern Wei dynasty for an Indian monk named Batuo.
